Find the global extrema of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+1$ on the closed region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\le 0,\,y\ge 0,\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 4\},$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
Since $f(x,y)$ is continuous on the closed, bounded region $D,$ the function attains a global maximum and minimum on $D.$

To find the extreme values, we follow three steps.

**Step 1.** Find the critical points of $f$ inside the region. 

To determine the critical points, we solve  ${f}^{′}=0.$ Computing the derivative gives

$$
{f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x,\,-2y\end{aligned}].
$$

The derivative exists at each point inside $D,$ and it equals zero when

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2x=0 \\ -2y=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}x=0 \\ y=0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us a single point $(0,0).$ Since the point $(0,0)$ does not belong to the interior of $D,$ we do not yet include it in the list of candidates for extrema (it lies on the boundary of $D,$ so we will consider it in the next step).

**Step 2.**  Find the points on the boundary of $D$ that could give rise to extreme values. 

To find the points on the boundary that could give rise to extreme values, we parametrize each part of the boundary:

- The line connecting $(-2,0)$ and $(0,0)$ can be parametrized as

$$
r=⟨t,0⟩,\,t\in (-2,0).
$$

The values of $f$ on this boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(t,0) \\  & =(t)^{2}-(0)^{2}+1 \\  & ={t}^{2}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the critical points of $F(t)$ on the open interval $t\in (-2,0),$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ ({t}^{2}+1)^{′} & =0 \\ 2t & =0 \\ t & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $t=0$ is not inside the interval $t\in (-2,0).$

- The line connecting $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$ can be parametrized as

$$
r=⟨0,t⟩,\,t\in (0,2).
$$

The values of $f$ on this boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(0,t) \\  & =(0)^{2}-(t)^{2}+1 \\  & =1-{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the critical points of $F(t)$ on the open interval $t\in (0,2),$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ (1-{t}^{2})^{′} & =0 \\ -2t & =0 \\ t & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $t=0$ is not inside the interval $t\in (0,2).$

- The quarter-circle connecting $(-2,0)$ and $(0,2)$ can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨t,\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}⟩,\,t\in (-2,0).\end{aligned}
$$

The values of $f$ on this boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(t,\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}) \\  & ={t}^{2}-(\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}})^{2}+1 \\  & =2{t}^{2}-3.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the critical points of $F(t)$ on the open interval $t\in (-2,0),$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ (2{t}^{2}-3)^{′} & =0 \\ 4t & =0 \\ t & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solution, $t=0$ is not inside the interval $t\in (-2,0).$

Also, we have to include the corner points of the region as candidates for extrema. So, we obtain three candidates on the boundary:

$$
(-2,0),\,(0,0),\,(0,2)
$$

**Step 3.** Evaluate $f(x,y)$ at each of the candidate points, and compare their values. 

Evaluating $f(x,y)$ at each of the points mentioned above, we get the following: 

| $(x,y)$ | $(0,0)$ | $(-2,0)$ | $(0,2)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x,y)$ | $1$ | $5$ | $-3$ |

Therefore, on the closed region $D,$ we have that 

- $f$ attains the global minimum of $-3$ at the points $(0,2),$ and

- $f$ attains the global maximum of $5$ at the point $(-2,0).$
